This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 9 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/chengdu/ZUUU.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Recent short-range forecasts show only modest day-to-day variability, with no significant tropical moisture or frontal systems expected to moderate temperatures tomorrow. The combined 84.5% market probability on 37–38°C therefore reflects trader assessment of these stable, high-pressure drivers and the narrow uncertainty band in the latest model runs.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Frequent southwest monsoon (habagat) rains and extensive cloud cover are the dominant factors capping maximum temperatures in Manila near 29–31°C on August 10.** PAGASA’s latest outlooks for Metro Manila list highs of 30°C with a 60% rain chance, consistent with recent model guidance showing widespread convection that limits solar heating. The past 24–48 hours have featured suppressed readings (e.g., 26.6°C observed on August 8) under active monsoon flow, reinforcing trader expectations that similar conditions will persist.

Urban heat-island effects in the densely built metro area can add 1–2°C locally during brief clear spells, creating the narrow spread between 29°C and 31°C outcomes. Historical August climatology centers on 31°C daytime peaks, but enhanced rainfall this season has kept recent daily maxima 1–2°C below average. With resolution hinging on the official PAGASA Port Area reading, traders are weighting the latest agency guidance and short-range model consensus most heavily; any reduction in monsoon activity or clearing skies before the 10th would quickly shift implied probabilities toward the upper end of the 29–31°C band.
